tools.name: fetch_markdown
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its main content as clean Markdown (nav, ads and boilerplate removed). Raw Markdown, plain-text and JSON endpoints are returned as-is. Use this to read an article, docs page or raw file.

tools.name: fetch_metadata
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its metadata as JSON: title, byline, site name, excerpt and word count (no full body).

tools.name: extract_links
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return all of its outbound http(s) links (with anchor text) as JSON. Useful for crawling or finding related pages.

tools.name: search_page
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return only the passages that match a query, instead of the whole page. Each result includes its heading breadcrumb and is ranked by relevance. Use this to find a specific detail (e.g. pricing, a config option) while spending far fewer tokens than fetch_markdown.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "fetch_markdown" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Fetch a web page and return its main content as clean Markdown (nav, ads and boilerplate removed). Use this to read an article or documentation page." → after: "Fetch a web page and return its main content as clean Markdown (nav, ads and boilerplate removed). Raw Markdown, plain-text and JSON endpoints are returned as-is. Use this to read an article, docs page or raw file."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
